## TL;DR

Moved Work board search into the desktop header, hid the Client board link on Work, and removed search from filter chips while preserving clear and URL-backed filtering. Kept the query visible and editable on Pipeline to avoid hidden active state. The latest scoped RepoOS check failed on remote WebKit inbox overflow tests.

## Work and rationale

The desktop header now groups the half-width search with the Human/Held controls and keeps the title in the same header row. The Client board route remains intact; only its Work-page link is hidden. Search remains synced to `q`, continues filtering the board, and is cleared by both the input's clear control and Clear filters. Search itself is excluded from chips; other filter chips and Clear filters remain.

Pipeline does not apply the board search, but continues to show the input so a retained query is visible and can be edited or cleared. The phone queue layout remains separate. Updated headless WebKit coverage exercises the real app shell at 375, 768, and 1280px and checks header alignment, collisions, and horizontal overflow. The Inbox fixture also uses the real sidebar and main shell; long unbroken task titles wrap instead of expanding the board beyond the viewport.

Integrated the branch with main, retaining the changes on both sides of the `workQueueFilters.ts` conflict. An earlier scoped check passed; the latest run failed on the remote runner's inbox overflow tests at 768 and 1280 pixels. Those cases passed locally.

## Approaches tried

Removing the search chip without changing Pipeline would hide a retained query while Pipeline was selected. Keeping its input visible makes the state inspectable and clearable without applying the query to Pipeline's columns.

The first inbox viewport fixture exposed horizontal overflow with many long task titles. Using the real shell in the fixture and allowing card content and titles to shrink/wrap addressed the same overflow class rather than weakening the viewport assertion.

## Challenges and blockers

The prior review identified a merge conflict, header alignment gaps in the fixture, and hidden search state on Pipeline. The merge is integrated; the updated fixtures exercise the real shell and the Pipeline input stays visible. The outdated landscape CSS assertion was corrected. A later turn added the missing search component's scoped CSS to the Inbox fixture and waited for the Work layout to switch after viewport changes. Those cases passed locally, but the scoped remote check still failed: WebKit reported document overflow with no element bounding box beyond the viewport. A subsequent diagnostic run traced the Inbox overflow to the native select inside the Work header actions; offline Work reports similar overflow. The worktree became read-only after the check, preventing a fix and verification.

The next review found that its screenshot and engineering report were bound to an older tree, and its landing checklist saw three uncommitted files. Those changes are now included in the branch tip and the worktree is clean. A new handoff is needed to capture the current tree, bind this report to it, and establish a fresh review lock; none of those server-owned artifacts can be represented as already complete here.

## Key learnings

Responsive layout fixtures should include the app's actual sidebar and content padding. URL-backed state needs to remain visible and editable even when the current view does not apply it.
